name: Nightshade
review: Works as a state on the defender once 9.6.3 gains one line for Health loss: it is recorded with damage taken (current Health = maximum − damage − loss), so healing restores it and a lost Health aura still counts it, but it is not a damage event, so Shell doesn't break, Knot doesn't share it, Bloodied, Bud, Grudge and Bitter Toad don't fire, and because it never takes the last point there is no kill to credit. Needs two rulings: halve as the first part of the damage exchange (9.6.1 step 3) rather than in step 1, so a dodged (Jink), redirected (Shoulder) or cancelled attack halves only the unit actually hit; and halve once per attack turn, so Peck (X) halves once (as Peck's review already proposes for the target's 'when attacked' effects), a Swarm joint attack halves once, and repeat or immediate attacks (9.4.11, 9.4.12) halve again. Under that ruling Swarm works against Nightshade, since bees attacking one by one halve more often than one swarm, so 'how they play' should drop Swarm unless the owner picks per-joiner halving; otherwise there is no loop or stall, a returning unit comes back clean (9.8.2), and the units read well, though Hornet Scout should print 'summon a 1/1 Hornetling that also attacks enemies with Nightshade', and Bitter Toad's mark lands after the current attack's halving, so it bites from the next attack. Answers to the designer's questions: Health loss that isn't damage: take the designer's proposal and write it into 9.6.3 as above. The rulebook has no healing rule yet, so 'can be healed like damage' should become 'healing restores lost Health and damage alike, up to maximum' when healing is written. Halving can't take a unit from 1 to 0, so no death check is needed after it and the kill always belongs to the hit. Peck (X): halve once per Peck attack. Peck's 'each strike counts as an attack' is for its own 'whenever this attacks' effects; the rules review of Peck already proposes that the target's 'when attacked' effects fire once. X halvings would make Peck 3 plus one applier take seven eighths of a unit in one turn, which is removal rather than the wide plan. If the owner wants the combo, it should be a line on a specific card ('your Peck strikes each count for Nightshade'), not the default. Swarm: one joint attack is one attack on the defender, so it halves once, before all the joiners' hits land together. That is consistent with Peck and with 9.6.1 running once per attack, but it means Swarm and Nightshade pull against each other; the entry should say so instead of listing Swarm as feeding the plan. Extra attacks: yes as written. Each repeat attack (9.4.11) and each 'attacks immediately' (9.4.12) runs its own 9.6.1 and halves again; this is the wide payoff the owner described and needs no new rule. Golden Bitter Toad's defensive mark: no rules issue either way. It only adds anything when the Toad is attacked (when the Toad attacks, its own damage already marks the defender), so it is a front-row trigger; giving it to every Toad pulls the Toad into the front row, keeping it golden-only keeps the Toad a back-row unit. A design call for the owner.

other_notes: Belladonna Sprite reads 'the enemy with the highest Health' at Start of Combat. Under 9.3.4 that is the board before hero powers; under R8's proposal it is the board when the Sprite resolves, so the random side order (9.3.2) decides whether an enemy Start of Combat buff changes who is highest. Either rule works; it should be one of them. 'Enemy' here is any row, as a described target (9.5.6).

Hornet Scout's preference is a targeting override (9.5.7). Place it after back-row protection and must-be-attacked in R6's order: it picks a Nightshaded unit only among the final candidates, so a marked back-row unit behind a living front row is ignored, and a Taunt-like unit still wins. Several marked candidates: random.
Bitter Toad: a hit that Shrug reduces to nothing deals no damage (R1), so it marks nothing; a hit capped by Shell still marks.
Bud copies and any other copy made in combat should not inherit Nightshade: it is a debuff from the enemy, not the card's text.

Variations: Nettled and Three Drops follow the same timing and counting rules (one per attack turn, at the start of step 3). Creeping Nightshade uses last-known positions (12.2.3) and same-row adjacency without skipping gaps (8.2.2); it can't loop, since Nightshade doesn't stack and each unit dies once.

Scene checked against 9.4.5 and 9.4.8: each Hornetling lands in its Scout's slot and attacks next as written, the boar's own attacks don't halve it, and 70, 34, 16, 7, 3, 1, dead in six 1-damage attacks is correct.
